mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0% (3-month average), or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tightening labor market that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in less than 40% of periods when UNRATE falls below 4.0%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer and business spending, driving near-term equity demand and positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in less than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS grow >0.5% MoM, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Weak supply growth (INDPRO below 100.5) signals production constraints that increase inflation expectations and trigger monetary tightening, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in less than 60% of periods when INDPRO growth is below 0.5% YoY, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity that supports corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in less than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY >2.5%) signals central bank tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in less than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 2.5%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous payroll growth (PAYEMS >0.3% MoM) and unemployment decline (UNRATE fall >0.1pp) indicate a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in less than 55% of periods when PAYEMS grows >0.3% MoM and UNRATE falls >0.1pp, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.0% over 3 months) increase discount rates and reduce liquidity, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in less than 60% of periods during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rise >4.0% over 3 months), or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
